page.layout: One column of numbered theses (XVI to XXIII) down the page, with the closing line of the last thesis at the foot. Below the text: signature "C" at left-centre and catchword "Non" at right. No running head, no page number, no margin notes.

main_text.p: Vel deniq; ipsius Reipublicæ, communissimi diuinissimiq; boni consequedi ratione cōsyderat, & præscribit. Πολιτικὴ [?] est illa Aristoteli καὶ [?] ἐξοχῶ [?] dicta. 1. Ethic. 2.

p.i: Vt igitur in hac Morali Philosophia varietas incidit, tum Graduū, tum etiam Mediorū: ita in varias quoq; partes illa fuit diducta: Ethica Generalis, Oeconomica, Politica.
Ista fundamenta iacit; hæc insuper disponit; ultima denique summam perfectionem & ornatum superinducit.
Virtus vero universè accepta, est forma perficiens id, cuius est virtus, & opus eius.

main_text.p: Ast cuius virtus humana perfectio dicitur, vel Appetitus brutus est, vel denique Ratio. 1. Ethicor. 13.
Appetitum brutum perficiunt & dirigunt Virtu-tes Morales, ἕξεις [?] comparatæ: Rationem vero, Virtutes i-psius Mentis, Dianoëticæ.

p.i: Virtus Moralis, hæc constituit Virum bonum, & ciuē itidem bonum. Rationalis in primis Sapientem informat & perficit.

main_text.p: Arctissimè autem inter sese coniuncta virtutes Mo-rales. Omnes enim à prudentia dependent: omnes rectâ ratione ad honestum contendunt, omnes etiā sæpe in mu-nerū suorū functione inter sese connectuntur. Haud in individuo: atqʒ idcirco omnes quoque nomine universæ Temperatiæ, universæq; Fortitudinis appellantur: ma-ximè tamen Iustitiæ universæ, quæ συλληβδὴν πᾶσ' ἀρε-τῆς [?] Lib. 5. Ethic. Nicom.

page.notes: Printing error: the heading XVIII is printed "XIIX." and is left as printed. Greek passages are transcribed from a small, slightly blurred print; the marked words (Πολιτικὴ, καὶ, ἐξοχῶ, ἕξεις, and the final Greek phrase) are doubtful. The initial glyph before "Morali" and before "Mediorū" is a decorative sign and was not reproduced. Catchword "Non" and signature "C" are at the foot.
